subject: mixed effects negative binomial: modeling count data

messages.author: e19ea506112fd25b
messages.subject: mixed effects negative binomial: modeling count data
parts:
Hi,

I am trying to model repeated measures overdispersed count data using mixed-effects negative binomial in rstan.  The model is attached.  For some reason I am receiving funny message (although convergence is good, good mixing, Rhat=1 and n_eff is reasonably large):
Informational Message: The current Metropolis proposal is about to be rejected becuase of the following issue:
Error in function boost::math::lgamma<e>(e): Evaluation of lgamma at a negative integer 0.

Any insight?

The R code is:
fit.nb.mix <- stan (file = "nbmix.stan", data = model.mix.dat,
    warmup = warmup, iter = warmup + n.draws, chains = 2)

Thanks for any clue,
Linas

messages.author: 3f22b207863d2049
messages.subject: Re: mixed effects negative binomial: modeling count data
parts:
Hi Linas,

To my understanding, this is not really an error but a more of a message. Apparently, the sampler got someplace very close to the bounds of the sampling space and tried stepping outside, resulting in a value that lgamma could not evaluate. This should not be bad if it only happens a few times. I haven't looked at the attachment, but make sure that the support for all your parameters is well defined and in line with the bounds on your priors (if there are any). You should only worry if you repeatedly get messages like this; this could (or always does?) indicate that the parameter support is ill-defined (ie the bounds on your parameters in the parameters block).

Luc

messages.subject: Re: mixed effects negative binomial: modeling count data
parts:
I took a quick look at the attachment and the model seemed to be ok (although I didn't understand the details of the likelihood). 

Just curious, are you eventually building a mixture model or using the likelihood for non-sampling purposes?
If not, you may want to just write

for (i in 1 : N) counts[i] ~ neg_binomial(shape, shape /  exp (alpha0 + alpha[loti[i]]));

in the model block. Also, I would use a prior like normal(0, 100) or cauchy(0, 100) for the variance or sigma parameter. That it gets cut at zero because the parameter is restricted to be above zero happens not to be a problem. 

The warnings you get during adaptation are ok if you don't get them all the time during sampling.

messages.author: 3f22b207863d2049
messages.subject: Re: mixed effects negative binomial: modeling count data
parts:
Being a rstan user, I haven't look at the .stan file, but I have an inkling what's causing these messages to appear in your case.

When you specify a prior uniform (0.1, 100), you should make sure that you also declare the parameter with <lower=0.1,upper=100> in the parameter block. If you don't, the sampler might still sample a value under 0.1 (or over 100) and evaluate that against uniform(0.1, 100), leading to the quoted message.
